docs.title: High-Integrity Stochastic Computation
docs.text: Vectra™ is a high-performance computational platform for finite-state stochastic-process computation and diagnostics. Designed for enterprise environments where numerical precision and structural validation are non-negotiable, Vectra provides a deterministic, embeddable runtime for complex Markovian models.

docs.title: Powered by ATGS Enterprise Core
docs.text: Vectra is built on the ATGS Enterprise Core, a C++20 engine specialized in continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) solvers. By separating the high-level platform experience from the underlying technical engine, Vectra delivers a stable, production-oriented evaluation environment for critical diagnostic workloads.

docs.title: Evaluation Services
docs.text: We offer two primary paths for technical evaluators to engage with the platform: - Vectra SDK: Embed the runtime into your own diagnostic pipelines for local evaluation. - Diagnostic Review: Submit representative workloads for a structured technical audit by our engineering team.

docs.title: The Vectra Standard
docs.text:
• Integrity First: Every model is validated against rigorous mathematical preconditions before computation begins.
  • Exact Solvers: Deterministic algorithms for first-passage times and transient distributions, avoiding the statistical noise of simulation-based methods.
  • Diagnostic Depth: Advanced analysis of process topology, stiffness, and irreducibility.
  • Embeddable Architecture: Designed for deep integration into simulation pipelines and diagnostic software.

docs.title: Vectra Diagnostic Review
docs.text:
As part of our commitment to technical excellence and evaluator trust, Yozi Systems Labs offers the Vectra Diagnostic Review—an early-stage technical evaluation service for organizations developing complex finite-state stochastic models.

Early diagnostic reviews may be available for qualified organizations evaluating finite-state stochastic-process workloads.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The Vectra Diagnostic Review is a structured technical assessment designed to help evaluators understand the numerical and structural properties of their models using the Vectra™ validation engine. This is a selective, founder-led service focused on technical verification, not open-ended consulting or advisory.

docs.title: What You Can Submit
docs.text: Organizations may submit representative samples of their stochastic workloads for review, including: - Transition Matrices: CTMC generator matrices in dense or sparse formats. - Stochastic Models: Finite-state process definitions and graph-based models. - CTMC Workloads: Production-style workloads requiring first-passage or transient analysis. - Diagnostic Cases: Models suspected of numerical instability or stiffness. - Evaluation Inputs: Benchmark-style inputs for performance and precision testing.

docs.title: Analysis Scope
docs.text: Leveraging the ATGS Enterprise Core runtime, we analyze your submission for: - Validation & Refusal Behavior: How the model interacts with high-integrity validation gates. - Matrix Integrity: Detailed audit of row-sum invariants and off-diagonal discipline. - Structural Classification: Analysis of absorbing, transient, and irreducible components. - Computability: Verification of first-passage and transient solver preconditions. - Numerical Risk: Identification of stiffness, ill-conditioning, and residual errors. - Integration Readiness: Assessment of how the model structure aligns with the Vectra SDK.

docs.title: What You Receive
docs.text: Following the review, you will receive a Structured Diagnostic Report containing: - Model Risk Audit: Identified numerical or topological risks. - Refusal Findings: Detailed explanation of any refusal or error codes triggered. - Numerical Observations: Insights into stiffness ratios and condition estimates. - Integration Recommendations: Suggested paths for embedding the runtime into your stack. - Next Evaluation Path: Recommendations for moving toward a full Pilot Program.

docs.title: Engagement Boundaries
docs.text:
• Selectivity: We evaluate submissions based on technical fit and availability. Acceptance for a review is not guaranteed.
  • Commercial Intent: A diagnostic review is an evaluation tool and does not constitute a guarantee of a long-term commercial engagement.
  • No Production Claims: Reports are for evaluation purposes only and do not constitute a claim of production readiness or regulated certification.
  • No Professional Advice: Vectra Diagnostic Reviews do not provide legal, financial, medical, or safety certification advice.

docs.title: Platform & Capabilities
docs.text: Vectra™ is a specialized runtime platform for the exact analysis of continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs) and complex graph-based processes, powered by the ATGS Enterprise Core engine.

docs.title: High-Integrity Validation Architecture
docs.text:
Vectra implements a unique "Validation-Refusal" architecture. Rather than producing potentially corrupted results on unstable or invalid models, Vectra rigorously validates every input.

  • Validation Discipline: Enforces row-sum invariants and off-diagonal non-negativity with extreme precision.
  • Structured Refusal: When a model fails validation, Vectra provides a programmatic refusal report, allowing calling systems to diagnose the failure without crashing.

docs.title: Advanced Solver Suite
docs.text: Vectra delivers exact numerical solutions where traditional simulations often fail to converge or provide sufficient precision.

docs.title: First-Passage Analysis
docs.text: Compute exact mean first-passage times (MFPT) and variances for absorbing processes. Vectra handles complex state-spaces to identify process completion probabilities and temporal reliability.

docs.title: Exact Transient Computation
docs.text: Calculate probability distributions at arbitrary time horizons using high-order uniformization. The underlying ATGS engine manages Poisson truncation and convergence tracking automatically.

docs.title: Stiffness Diagnostics
docs.text: Vectra identifies "stiff" models—those with extreme exit-rate disparities—and provides diagnostic flags to ensure the numerical integrity of the results is maintained.

docs.title: Embeddable Runtime Architecture
docs.text:
The Vectra platform is delivered as an embeddable SDK, centered around the stable ATGS C ABI. This ensures that the high-performance C++20 runtime can be integrated into nearly any environment—from Python-based research pipelines to production C/C++ diagnostic systems—without exposing internal implementation details.

For technical specifications or evaluation requests, contact info@yozi.systems.

docs.title: Current Vectra Roadmap
docs.text: Vectra™ is an evolving platform. Our roadmap is focused on enhancing the depth, performance, and reach of the underlying ATGS Enterprise Core while maintaining absolute numerical integrity.

docs.title: Current Platform State (v0.7A)
docs.text: The current release provides a stable foundation for high-integrity stochastic computation: * Exact MFPT and variance solvers for absorbing CTMCs. * Uniformization-based transient distribution solvers. * The primary ATGS C ABI and Python wrapper. * Initial stiffness and numerical instability diagnostics. * Structured refusal/validation architecture.

docs.title: Near-Term Priorities
docs.text: Focusing on integration ergonomics and diagnostic depth: * Enhanced Topology Engine: Improved classification of complex state-spaces and irreducible components. * Expanded CLI Functionality: Richer JSON reporting for performance metrics and stiffness analysis. * SDK Polish: Improved header layout and C-minimal integration examples for common toolchains.

docs.title: Mid-Term Expansion
docs.text: Extending the solver engine's capabilities: * Sparse-Matrix Optimizations: Improved memory and performance profiles for extremely large, sparse state-spaces. * Sensitivity Analysis: Tools to analyze how small changes in exit rates impact first-passage and transient results. * Advanced Numerical Stability: Even more granular diagnostics for edge-case state classifications.

docs.title: Long-Term Platform Direction
docs.text:
Ensuring Vectra remains the standard for stochastic runtime integrity: * Domain-Specific Diagnostic Adapters: Streamlining integration for reliability engineering and network process analysis. * Platform Broadening: Expanded support for enterprise-standard deployment environments. * Collaborative Design-Partner Features: Integrating feedback from our Pilot Program to solve real-world stochastic modeling challenges.

Vectra is technically focused and evaluator-driven. For feature requests or pilot discussions: info@yozi.systems.

docs.title: Why Vectra?
docs.text: Vectra™ was designed to solve a specific problem in enterprise diagnostics: the failure of traditional stochastic methods to provide the rigor and deterministic reliability required for high-stakes decision-making.

docs.title: Exact CTMC Computation
docs.text: Unlike simulation-based tools that rely on Monte Carlo sampling and suffer from "stochastic noise," Vectra implements exact numerical solvers for continuous-time Markov chains. This ensures that every result is a precise mathematical solution, not a statistical estimate.

docs.title: Validation over Silent Corruption
docs.text: Most computational engines will attempt to solve any input, often producing corrupted results if the model is ill-conditioned or mathematically invalid. Vectra enforces a strict Validation/Refusal discipline: if a model does not meet the necessary preconditions, the runtime refuses the computation and provides a structured report explaining why.

docs.title: Deterministic Diagnostics
docs.text: Reproducibility is core to the Vectra philosophy. Given the same input, Vectra will always produce the same exact result. This deterministic behavior is critical for regression testing, process validation, and regulatory compliance in diagnostic pipelines.

docs.title: Embeddable Architecture
docs.text: Vectra is not a monolithic application. It is a lean, high-performance runtime delivered as an SDK. By utilizing the stable ATGS C ABI boundary, Vectra can be embedded deep into existing software stacks without introducing complex dependencies or exposing proprietary C++ internals.

docs.title: Integration Ergonomics
docs.text: From the opaque context management to the caller-owned buffer pattern, every aspect of the Vectra SDK is designed for integration safety. We prioritize a clean, predictable API that minimizes the risk of memory leaks or threading issues in host applications.

docs.title: Evaluator Trust
docs.text:
We believe that engineers should trust their computational tools. By providing stiffness diagnostics, convergence tracking, and explicit numerical flags, Vectra gives evaluators the transparency they need to verify the integrity of their stochastic models. Organizations can further verify this through a Vectra Diagnostic Review.

Built for engineers who value precision over approximation. Inquiries: info@yozi.systems

docs.title: Vectra SDK
docs.text: The Vectra SDK provides the libraries, headers, and tools required to embed the Vectra™ runtime into your own diagnostic and simulation applications.

docs.title: Integration Surfaces
docs.text: The SDK is built to provide maximum stability while maintaining the performance of the underlying ATGS Enterprise Core.

docs.title: ATGS C ABI (Primary)
docs.text: The technical foundation of the SDK is the stable ATGS C ABI. This pure-C boundary ensures that the Vectra runtime can be integrated into virtually any language or environment with binary stability.

docs.title: Python Wrapper
docs.text: A high-level binding built on top of the ATGS C ABI, providing a seamless experience for Python-based diagnostic and simulation pipelines.

docs.title: Vectra CLI
docs.text: A JSON-in / JSON-out command-line tool suitable for rapid model prototyping and automated pipeline integration.

docs.title: ATGS Enterprise Core — ABI Compatibility and Versioning
Current ABI Version
docs.text: Field Value SOVERSION 0 VERSION 0.7.0 Library name (Linux) libatgs_core_c.so.0 Library name (macOS) libatgs_core_c.0.dylib Header include/atgs/atgs_core_c.h

docs.title: ABI Boundary
docs.text:
The public ABI consists of: - The opaque context handle: ATGS_Context* - The status code enum: ATGS_StatusCode - The timing struct: ATGS_TimingSummary - Exported C functions

What does NOT cross the ABI: - C++ types, templates, or exceptions - Eigen matrix types - STL containers (std::vector, std::string, etc.) - Private runtime headers

The ABI is pure C. It is compatible with C89 callers and C++ callers via extern "C".

docs.title: SOVERSION (binary compatibility)
docs.text:
SOVERSION increments only when the ABI breaks. An ABI break means: - Removing or renaming an exported function - Changing the parameter list or return type of a function - Changing the size or layout of ATGS_TimingSummary - Removing or renumbering ATGS_StatusCode values

Consumers linked against SOVERSION 0 are guaranteed compatible with any libatgs_core_c.so.0.x.y that shares the same SOVERSION.

docs.title: ABI-safe additions (no SOVERSION bump)
docs.text:
• Adding new exported functions with new names
  • Adding new ATGS_StatusCode values at unused numeric positions
  • Adding new fields to ATGS_TimingSummary at the end (if padded)

docs.title: Long-Term Integration Guidance
docs.text:
• Link against libatgs_core_c.so (development symlink) at build time.
  • Deploy libatgs_core_c.so.0 and libatgs_core_c.so.0.7.0 at runtime.
  • Do not embed private include/atgs/*.hpp headers — they are not ABI-stable and are not part of the public interface.
  • All future external integration routes through the C ABI only.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: atgs_cli --input <path> [--output <path>] [--pretty]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --input <path> Required. Path to a JSON input file. --output <path> Optional. Write JSON output to this file. Default: stdout. --pretty Optional. Pretty-print JSON output with 2-space indentation.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success, or a structured computation refusal (both produce valid JSON output) 1 JSON parse error, missing --input, or unreadable file 2 Unhandled internal error

Note: structured refusals (e.g., no absorbing states, invalid generator) exit 0 and produce a JSON refusal report. Callers must inspect "status" in the output to distinguish success from refusal.

docs.title: Generator matrix (one required)
docs.text:
Dense matrix format: 

{
  "generator_matrix": [
    [-4.0, 4.0],
    [ 0.0, 0.0]
  ]
}

Sparse edge-list format: 

{
  "n_states": 3,
  "edges": [
    [0, 1, 2.0],
    [1, 2, 3.0]
  ]
}

docs.title: Solver requests
docs.text: Key Type Default Description request_first_passage bool true Compute absorbing FPT mean and variance request_entropy_production bool false Compute steady-state entropy production (irreducible only) request_transient_distribution bool false Compute p(t) = p₀·exp(Qt) time_horizon float — Required when transient requested initial_distribution float array — Required when transient requested

docs.title: Output Format (JSON)
docs.text:
Key top-level fields:

Field Description status "ok" or "refused" generator_summary Validation result, state counts, irreducibility absorption_summary FPT results (if computed) performance_summary Timings, solver path, residuals refused_quantities List of quantities that could not be computed numerical_flags List of active numerical warnings

docs.title: ATGS Enterprise Core — SDK Integration Guide
Integration Paths
docs.text:
Path Use case Shared library (lib/libatgs_core_c.so) Dynamic linking — preferred for most integrations Static library Embedded or single-binary deployments CLI (bin/atgs_cli) Pipeline integration, scripting, evaluation Python wrapper Python consumers (requires source build via pybind11)

All paths route through the same stable C ABI (include/atgs/atgs_core_c.h).

docs.title: C/C++ Linking — Shared Library
docs.text:
Headers: include/atgs/atgs_core_c.h

Library: lib/libatgs_core_c.so (Linux) or lib/libatgs_core_c.dylib (macOS)

docs.title: gcc / clang
docs.text:
gcc -I /path/to/sdk/include \
    your_program.c \
    /path/to/sdk/lib/libatgs_core_c.so \
    -o your_program

# Run with rpath or LD_LIBRARY_PATH:
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/path/to/sdk/lib ./your_program

docs.title: CMake (standalone consumer)
docs.text:
add_executable(my_app main.c)
target_include_directories(my_app PRIVATE /path/to/sdk/include)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE /path/to/sdk/lib/libatgs_core_c.so)

docs.title: Context Lifecycle
docs.text:
#include "atgs/atgs_core_c.h"

ATGS_Context* ctx = ATGS_CreateContext();
// ... perform operations ...
ATGS_FreeContext(ctx);   // always free; no automatic lifetime management

One context per logical compute thread. Not thread-safe across threads.

docs.title: Calling Convention
docs.text:
All operations take a flat, row-major double array for the generator matrix. Output arrays are pre-allocated by the caller.

// n-state CTMC: Q is a double[n*n] in row-major order
double Q[n * n] = { ... };

// Outputs must be pre-allocated to length n
double mean[n], variance[n];

ATGS_StatusCode status =
    ATGS_SolveFirstPassage(ctx, Q, n, mean, variance, n);

docs.title: Status Code Categories
docs.text:
Range Meaning 0 Success 100–109 Structured refusal (computation rejected, not a crash) 200–299 Caller error (null pointer, bad argument, buffer too small)

Always check the return value. Structured refusals (100–109) are expected and recoverable — they carry diagnostic information via ATGS_GetLastErrorMessage.

docs.title: Error Retrieval
docs.text:
if (status != ATGS_STATUS_SUCCESS) {
    char msg[512];
    ATGS_GetLastErrorMessage(ctx, msg, sizeof(msg));
    fprintf(stderr, "status %d: %s\n", (int)status, msg);
}

docs.title: Timing
docs.text:
ATGS_TimingSummary timing;
ATGS_GetLastTimingSummary(ctx, &timing);
printf("total: %.2f ms\n", timing.total_ms);

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
ATGS Enterprise Core is a finite-state stochastic-process runtime implementing exact continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) solvers. It is distributed as a commercial software platform for pilot evaluation and integration testing.

Public integration surfaces: - C ABI — stable, pure-C shared/static library (include/atgs/atgs_core_c.h) - Python wrapper — pybind11 module layered on the C ABI (build from source) - CLI — JSON-in / JSON-out command-line tool (bin/atgs_cli)

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text:
./bin/atgs_cli --input <path/to/input.json> [--output <path>] [--pretty]

Exit codes: 0 = success or structured refusal, 1 = parse/argument error, 2 = internal error

Quick example — absorbing CTMC first-passage:

./bin/atgs_cli --input examples/cli/absorbing_fpt.json --pretty

Expected result includes mean_fpt[0] = 0.25, variance_fpt[0] = 0.0625. See sample_outputs/absorbing_fpt_output.json for the full output in the SDK bundle.

docs.title: C ABI Linking
docs.text:
See docs/SDK_INTEGRATION.md for complete linking instructions and the minimal C example in examples/c_minimal/.

One-liner (gcc, Linux):

gcc -I include/ examples/c_minimal/main.c lib/libatgs_core_c.so \
    -o my_atgs_app
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=lib ./my_atgs_app

docs.title: Input Schema
docs.text:
See docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md or the formal schema in schemas/atgs_input_v1.schema.json. Key top-level keys:

Key Type Notes generator_matrix n×n array OR use edges + n_states edges [[i,j,rate], ...] sparse edge-list format n_states int required with edges request_first_passage bool default true request_entropy_production bool default false request_transient_distribution bool default false time_horizon float required when transient requested initial_distribution float array required when transient requested

docs.title: Build from Source (Internal)
docs.text:
Requires CMake 3.22+, C++20 compiler. Dependencies (Eigen, JSON, GTest) are fetched automatically during the first configure.

# SDK build (shared lib + examples):
cmake -S . -B build_sdk -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DATGS_BUILD_SHARED=ON -DATGS_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON
cmake --build build_sdk
ctest --test-dir build_sdk

# Default developer build:
cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build

docs.title: ATGS Enterprise Core — Refusal and Error Code Reference
docs.text: ATGS Enterprise Core uses structured status codes to communicate why a computation was either refused (rejected based on input properties) or errored (caller or system failure).

docs.title: Structured Refusals (100–199)
docs.text:
Refusals are expected and recoverable. They indicate that the input does not meet the mathematical or logical preconditions for the requested solver.

Code Name Meaning 100 ATGS_STATUS_REFUSED_INVALID_GENERATOR The matrix is not a valid CTMC generator (e.g., non-square, NaNs). 101 ATGS_STATUS_REFUSED_NEGATIVE_OFFDIAG An off-diagonal entry Q[i,j] is negative (tolerance: 1e-12). 102 ATGS_STATUS_REFUSED_ROW_SUM A row does not sum to zero (relative tolerance: 1e-10). 103 ATGS_STATUS_REFUSED_MISSING_INITIAL_DISTRIBUTION Transient distribution requested but initial_distribution is missing. 104 ATGS_STATUS_REFUSED_INVALID_TIME_HORIZON time_horizon is missing, negative, or zero. 105 ATGS_STATUS_REFUSED_NUMERICAL_INSTABILITY The solver encountered a singular or ill-conditioned system. 106 ATGS_STATUS_REFUSED_NO_ABSORBING_STATES First-passage requested but the CTMC has no absorbing states. 107 ATGS_STATUS_REFUSED_ALL_ABSORBING First-passage requested but all states are absorbing. 108 ATGS_STATUS_REFUSED_INITIAL_DISTRIBUTION_SUM initial_distribution does not sum to 1.0 (tolerance: 1e-8). 109 ATGS_STATUS_REFUSED_TRANSIENT_CONVERGENCE_FAILED Uniformization failed to converge within Poisson term limits.

docs.title: Caller and System Errors (200–299)
docs.text:
Errors indicate a violation of the API contract or a failure in the environment.

Code Name Meaning 200 ATGS_STATUS_ERROR_NULL_POINTER A required pointer argument (e.g., ctx, q_matrix) was NULL. 201 ATGS_STATUS_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT A non-pointer argument (e.g., n_states == 0) was invalid. 202 ATGS_STATUS_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL A caller-provided output buffer was too small for the result. 299 ATGS_STATUS_ERROR_INTERNAL An unhandled exception or logic error occurred inside the runtime.

docs.title: Handling Strategy
docs.text:
1. Success (0): Proceed with results.
  2. Refusal (100–199): Do not proceed. Report the diagnostic message from ATGS_GetLastErrorMessage to the user or adjust the input. These are not "crashes."
  3. Error (200–299): Fix the calling code. These indicate bugs in the integration layer.
